title: Surviving Cancer Is Only Half the Battle
hook: More people than ever survive cancer — but the anxiety, depression, and guilt can linger for years after treatment ends, and often go unrecognized.
key_points: Better treatment and screening mean more Americans now survive cancer.
Many survivors carry lasting mental health effects — anxiety, depression, and guilt — for years.
These struggles often go unrecognized once active treatment ends.
Survivorship care increasingly means tending to mental health, not just scans and bloodwork.
content_html: Thanks to better treatment and earlier screening, more Americans survive cancer than ever — a genuine triumph. But survival is only part of the story. Many people finish treatment carrying lasting mental health burdens: anxiety, depression, and even guilt that can persist for years.
extra_html: These struggles often slip under the radar, because the medical focus shifts back to scans and bloodwork once the cancer is gone. The emerging message is that survivorship care should include mental health — and that survivors who feel persistently low, anxious, or adrift should treat that as a real, treatable part of recovery, not a personal failing. Reported by NPR.

related.title: Recognizing Depression and Anxiety
related.hook: Depression and anxiety are among the most common — and most treatable — health conditions. Knowing the signs is the first step to getting help that works.

related.title: Getting Help for Mental Health
related.hook: Mental health treatment works for most people — and the hardest part is usually just starting. Here's how to take the first step.

flashcards.explanation_html: As more people survive cancer, many are left with lasting anxiety, depression, and guilt — challenges that can persist for years and often go undiagnosed.

flashcards.prompt: Why do survivors' mental health struggles often go undiagnosed?
flashcards.back_html: Once active treatment ends, care tends to focus on scans and bloodwork — so lingering anxiety, depression, and guilt can slip under the radar.

flashcards.prompt: What's the emerging message about survivorship care?
flashcards.back_html: It should tend to mental health, not just physical follow-ups — persistent low mood or anxiety is a real, treatable part of recovery, not a personal failing.
